data.$comment: ZenSight types shared by several contracts: zs.thresholds.v1 and zs.desired.v1 must agree on ThresholdsConfig, so both list this file unchanged (Gap G12). Faithful to zensight-common/src/threshold.rs, comparison.rs, alert.rs (AlertSeverity) and desired.rs (AppliedConfig).

Ack.description: A write landed. v1 declared Ack without a schema ('ad-hoc JSON on the wire', zensight-common/src/schema.rs:225). In zk2 success is a value reply and failure a reply_err (O3), so nothing but an optional note remains.

AppliedConfig.description: What is actually in force for one reconcilable topic, and why (desired.v1's observed revision: desired_timestamp).

desired_timestamp.description: HLC timestamp of the applied desired sample (source = desired only).

effective_json.description: The document in force, JSON-encoded as a string. Its real type is the topic's.

topic.description: Repeats the key's {topic} (migration debt; tcgui gap 1).

ComparisonOp.description: Serialized in PascalCase (no serde rename); default GreaterThan.

timestamp.description: The rejected sample's HLC timestamp, when it carried one.

clear.description: Value hysteresis, on the quiet side of value.

labels.description: Label globs, all of which must match. v1 proxies matched `source` here; a device service no longer needs to.

metric.description: Glob over the resource path the service publishes (`if/*/in_errors.rate`). Under zk2 the paths change (the device leaves for the service name, rest families move under metrics/), so v1 rule sets need rewriting (migration debt).

name.description: Stable identity; becomes the alarm rule `threshold:<name>`.

ThresholdsConfig.description: The whole rule set one service evaluates, set wholesale (#928, #931). Every field is serde-defaulted.

data.$comment: telemetry.v1's standard schema (spec/profiles/telemetry/v1.md §2.3, §3; core §10 point 1). A contract lists this file, or a copy whose JCS bytes are equal, and a type is the profile's by this artifact's id, never by its name alone. The Point carries one measurement of any kind; a bare value carries a declared kind (§2.4). Every keyword inside telemetry.v1.Value's oneOf, and inside telemetry.v1.Histogram, which a branch reaches, is the pre-profile file's: changing one would be review (core §9.8). Descriptions and comments are annotations (core §7.3).

telemetry.v1.Epoch.description: An in-band continuity epoch (§2.9): an opaque string, compared for equality, which the owner changes whenever a counter or histogram it carries restarts. A Point carries it as epoch; a bare counter or histogram as an attachment of this type.

telemetry.v1.Histogram.description: Fixed buckets (§2.8): buckets are the bounds, strictly ascending and finite, upper-inclusive, +Inf implicit, equal by value to the resource's telemetry.buckets; counts is per bucket, not cumulative, one longer than buckets, the overflow last; count is their sum; counts and count never decrease within one epoch (§2.9), sum may.

telemetry.v1.Point.description: One measurement of one member (§2.3). The series is the key, never a label (§2.12).

labels.description: Context, never identity (§2.12): an OID, an interface description, an unslugged path. A label named unit is context too, not the member's unit (§2.5).

timestamp.description: The measurement time, Unix epoch milliseconds: when the value was taken, not when it was published (§2.12). A rate is timed by it (§2.11).

unit.description: The member's unit when its resource declares none (§2.5): 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters, compared byte for byte (§2.2). Absent means unknown, never dimensionless. A declared telemetry.unit is authoritative, and a Point that disagrees does not conform (§2.6).

telemetry.v1.Value.description: Internally tagged, {"type": <kind>, "value": ...}: the tag is a kind of §2.2, spelled as telemetry.kind spells it. Where the resource declares a kind, it is authoritative, and a tag that differs does not conform (§2.5, §2.6).

value.description: Bytes as an array of byte values, in JSON and in CBOR alike (§2.4).

data.$comment: sysinfo's own documents, faithful to zensight-common/src/gpu.rs, timesync.rs and query_detail.rs (ProcessRecord, LatencyReport). Telemetry points are telemetry.v1.json's.

LatencyHistogram.description: query_detail.rs `Histogram` (renamed here: telemetry.v1.Histogram is a different shape).

available.description: False when the eBPF collector could not load; the histograms are then empty.

cmdline.description: Scrubbed of secret-looking argv values and truncated (#302).

source.description: The time daemon consulted (chrony, timesyncd, ntpd, none).

data.description: zs.sysinfo.v1's frame record (core sections 7.6, 7.7; telemetry.v2; #1149 Z2): its untemplated readings, and its closed families flattened, one field each, named by the reading's template with / and . as _. Every field is optional: an owner writes a reading it does not have absent, never 0. A range and a resolution are the quantity's own bound where it has one, else a stated guess (examples/zk2/zensight/README.md, "Frames"). A counter's width holds its worst rate over 900 s, two keyframes apart at a frame a minute.
